evidence.claim: The evaluated BB-code family uses a fixed polynomial pair A(x,y)=x^3+y+y^2 and B(x,y)=y^3+x+x^2 across [[72,12,6]], [[108,8,10]], and [[144,12,12]] instances, keeping local check geometry and weight fixed while varying lattice size and distance.
evidence.locator: Section III.A, code specification and circuit build

evidence.claim: The benchmark runs use syndrome cycles equal to code distance, compare 2EC and 4EC schedules, sweep erasure rate e with p=0.1e and q=e, and decode using BP+OSD with fixed settings after Stim simulation.

At low erasure rate, increasing distance from 6 to 10 reduces per-round logical error by roughly 26-34x, while 10 to 12 gives a smaller 2.0-2.7x reduction; 4EC substantially narrows the Approx-versus-Exact engine gap.
